items.title: [Slice D] Standards crosswalk: W3C PROV-O, QIF (ISO 23952), STEP AP242 (ISO 10303-242)
items.body:
Handling: Unclassified — public

Part of #3.

## Why this matters

Industry already records manufacturing and quality data in established standards. A schema that maps cleanly to them can be adopted without re-keying data; one that does not will stay a research artefact.

## The problem

Map the OpenChokepoint v0.2.1 digital-thread types and links to existing provenance and manufacturing-data standards, and show the mapping working.

## Scope

1. **Crosswalk** (`docs/standards-crosswalk.md`): for each type and link (Component, SerialItem, MaterialLot, ProcessStep, EvidenceRecord, CriticalItem; instance_of, made_from, underwent, evidenced_by, performed_at, alternate_for), the closest concept in:
   - **W3C PROV-O** (provenance ontology);
   - **QIF** (Quality Information Framework, ISO 23952), for inspection and quality evidence;
   - **STEP AP242** (ISO 10303-242), for part identity and revision.
   Mark each mapping as exact, partial or none, with the reason.
2. **PROV-O export** (`tools/export_prov.py`): converts any trace to PROV-O (Turtle or JSON-LD) and passes a standard RDF parser.
3. **Gaps and proposals:** where the standards express something the schema cannot (or the reverse), propose changes for discussion. Do not change the schema in this slice.

## Acceptance test

- Every v0.2.1 type and link appears in the crosswalk.
- `tools/export_prov.py` converts the synthetic example, and the output parses in CI.
- Standards are cited by number and section only. No standard text is copied into the repository.

## Sample before full work

The crosswalk rows for EvidenceRecord and ProcessStep, as a draft PR.

## Before assignment

Comment here with your background and your named Responsible Person (CLA.md section 11). A maintainer assigns the slice; a `/take` comment is not an assignment. Bounty tier is posted before assignment (BOUNTIES.md).

## Good fit

Ontology and data modellers, manufacturing-data and model-based-enterprise specialists, quality-systems engineers.

items.title: Help us test the DSH web sidebar in a real DSH host
items.body:
## Why

The DSH plugin's four UI surfaces — sidebar footer action, conversation tab,
right-pane panel, and settings — have **never been mounted in a live DSH
runtime**. Everything we have is:

- TypeScript compilation
- unit tests
- static contract conformance (`scripts/check_dsh_plugin_contract.py`, 27/27 checks)

The README says this out loud (its honesty note in the DSH Plugin section:
verified for compile/unit/contract, **not** run against a live DSH runtime),
and `docs/compatibility.md` has every cell of the version matrix marked
unrun. There is no DSH host and no `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in this development
environment, so we cannot close that gap ourselves.

We need someone with a real DSH web host to tell us what actually happens.

## What to do

Install the plugin in a real DSH web host. Both documented install paths
work — use whichever matches your setup:

```bash
dsh plugin add pr-genius
```

or apply the one-line patch in [`cordis.patch.yml`](../../blob/main/cordis.patch.yml)
(see the "Install" subsection of the README's DSH Plugin section).

Then report on three things:

- **(a) Do the four surfaces appear?** sidebar footer action, conversation
  tab, right-pane panel, settings. Which ones render, and which don't?
- **(b) Any `service "..." is not declared by your plugin` errors?** These
  would come from the DSH guard rejecting a read of an undeclared service.
  Quote the exact message if you see one.
- **(c) Does the `/pr-genius` command respond?** Any output at all, or
  silence?

## Report template

Paste this and fill it in:

```
DSH version:
DSH / cordis SDK version:
install path used: (dsh plugin add | cordis.patch.yml)
host type: (web | other)

surfaces observed:
  [ ] sidebar footer action
  [ ] conversation tab
  [ ] right-pane panel
  [ ] settings

guard errors (exact text, or "none"):
  ...

/pr-genius command: (responds | silent | error: ...)

anything else that looked wrong:
  ...
```

## Please note your DSH/SDK version

This matters more than it sounds: the pinned SDK and upstream master
disagree on the slot catalog — **42 vs 92 keys**. A surface that lands on
`details` in one catalog may need `sidebar.right.pane.tab` in the other, so
a report without a version string is hard to act on.

## Related

- #100 — the registration bug being fixed (optional seats must be read
  through `ctx.get()` with an empty `inject`, not declared as hard
  requirements)
- #71 — the missing end-to-end verification this issue is asking you to
  help supply

items.title: [$25 BOUNTY] [Python] Add independent log parser fixtures
items.body:
**Bounty:** $25 (LT)

**Area:** `tools/log_aggregator.py` and parser fixture tests

**Current state:** The legacy log aggregator notes that parser tests can false-pass because the test data was generated by the same parser logic. This leaves JSON, text, and nginx log parsing vulnerable to regressions when real archived log formats drift.

**What's needed:** Add independent parser fixtures based on hand-written representative log lines and cover the main parser paths without relying on parser-generated samples. Keep the change focused on parser validation and do not change production parsing behavior unless a fixture exposes a clear bug.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add independent fixtures for JSON, plain text, and nginx-style log lines.
- Add focused tests or a validation script that verifies parser output for timestamp, level, service/format, and key fields.
- Include at least one malformed/unsupported line case that should not crash parsing.
- Existing log aggregation CLI behavior remains compatible.
- PR description explains the fixture source/intent and validation performed.

**Required validation:**
- Run `python3 build.py`
- Include the generated diagnostic `.logd` artifact from `diagnostic/build-XXX.logd` in the PR; also include `diagnostic/build-XXX.json` if present
- Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` for your submission

items.title: [BOUNTY $200] WORKFLOW: n8n + Claude Code — automated weekly dev summary
items.body:
## 💰 Bounty: $200 — powered by [Opire](https://opire.dev)

## Description
Create a complete n8n workflow that automatically generates a weekly narrative
summary of a GitHub repo's activity, using the Claude API.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exportable n8n workflow (importable `.json` file)
- [ ] Trigger: weekly cron (e.g., Friday at 5pm)
- [ ] Fetches from GitHub API: commits, closed issues, merged PRs for the week
- [ ] Calls Claude API (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`) to generate a narrative summary
- [ ] Delivers the summary via: email OR Discord/Slack webhook (your choice, documented)
- [ ] Configurable variables: GitHub repo, destination channel, language (EN/FR)
- [ ] Tested on a real n8n instance (include a screenshot of successful execution)
- [ ] README with setup instructions in 5 steps or fewer

## How to Claim
1. Comment `/opire try` in this issue
2. Submit a PR with the `.json` workflow + README
3. Payment is released automatically on merge ✅

## Resources
- n8n docs: https://docs.n8n.io
- Claude API docs: https://docs.anthropic.com
